Title: Can AI Solve the Peer Review Crisis? A Large Scale Cross Model Experiment of LLMs' Performance and Biases in Evaluating over 1000 Economics Papers
Authors: Pat Pataranutaporn, Nattavudh Powdthavee, Chayapatr Achiwaranguprok, Pattie Maes
Abstract summary: Large language models can reliably evaluate the quality of economics research, but exhibit human-like biases towards author gender and institutional affiliation.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Peer Review: Enhancing Efficiency While Preserving Integrity
Authors: B. Doskaliuk, O. Zimba, Marlen Yessirkepov, Iryna Klishch, R. Yatsyshyn
Abstract summary: AI can enhance the efficiency of peer review, but its limitations in understanding complex scientific content mean it should be used as a supportive tool, not a replacement for human expertise.

Title: Automated Research Review Support Using Machine Learning, Large Language Models, and Natural Language Processing
Authors: Vishnu S. Pendyala, Karnavee Kamdar, Kapil Mulchandani
Abstract summary: The paper describes a system that uses machine learning and language models to predict the quality and acceptance of research papers, and to recommend reviewers, in order to support the peer review process.

Title: Can LLM feedback enhance review quality? A randomized study of 20K reviews at ICLR 2025
Authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng, Fei Sha, Rose Yu, Carl Vondrick, James Zou
Abstract summary: An AI-based system that provides feedback to peer reviewers can enhance review quality and engagement between reviewers and authors.

Title: How Artificial Intelligence Differs From Humans in Peer Review.
Authors: Michael V. Joachim, Thomas B. Dodson, A. Laviv
Venue: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
Abstract summary: AI models are less likely to recommend rejection of research papers than human reviewers, suggesting they are better suited as screening tools rather than replacements for expert human peer review.

Title: Can AI help authors prepare better risk science manuscripts?
Authors: Louis Anthony Cox, T. Aven, Seth D. Guikema, Charles N. Haas, James H Lambert, Karen Lowrie, George Maldonado, Felicia Wu
Abstract summary: The paper evaluates two AI systems that provide feedback to authors on whether their draft papers fit a journal's guidelines and offer substantive technical feedback, with mixed results.

Title: Would Artificial Intelligence, Like ChatGPT, Be a Good ‘Peer’ Reviewer in Academic Publishing? A Human Versus AI-Based SWOT Assessment
Authors: J. A. Teixeira da Silva, Panagiotis Tsigaris
Abstract summary: The paper assesses the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of using AI like ChatGPT as a peer reviewer for academic publishing, concluding that AI has not yet reached a dependable stage for this task.

Title: Evaluating the predictive capacity of ChatGPT for academic peer review outcomes across multiple platforms
Authors: Mr. Thelwall, Abdallah Yaghi
Abstract summary: ChatGPT can produce weak predictions of peer review outcomes, but its effectiveness varies across platforms and the optimal input strategies differ.

Title: Enhancing peer review efficiency: A mixed‐methods analysis of artificial intelligence‐assisted reviewer selection across academic disciplines
Authors: Shai Farber
Abstract summary: AI-assisted reviewer selection can improve efficiency but requires human oversight to address limitations in understanding disciplinary contexts.

Title: AI-Driven Review Systems: Evaluating LLMs in Scalable and Bias-Aware Academic Reviews
Authors: Keith Tyser, Ben Segev, Gaston Longhitano, Xin-Yu Zhang, Zachary Meeks, Jason Lee, Uday Garg, Nicholas Belsten, A. Shporer, Madeleine Udell, Dov Te’eni, Iddo Drori
Abstract summary: This paper evaluates the use of large language models (LLMs) for automated academic paper reviewing, including their ability to predict human preferences and identify paper errors.

Title: Evaluating science: A comparison of human and AI reviewers
Authors: Anna Shcherbiak, Hooman Habibnia, Robert Böhm, Susann Fiedler
Abstract summary: AI could potentially be used as a prescreening tool for scientific abstracts, but has lower agreement with human reviewers compared to human-human agreement.

Title: The AI Review Lottery: Widespread AI-Assisted Peer Reviews Boost Paper Scores and Acceptance Rates
Authors: Giuseppe Russo, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Tim R. Davidson, Veniamin Veselovsky, Robert West
Abstract summary: AI-assisted peer reviews in machine learning conferences are prevalent, score higher than human reviews, and increase paper acceptance rates.

Title: Peer Review in the Age of Generative AI
Authors: A. Kankanhalli
Abstract summary: The paper discusses the potential for AI to augment the peer review process, as well as the associated pitfalls and implications for IS research.

Title: What Can Natural Language Processing Do for Peer Review?
Authors: Ilia Kuznetsov, Osama Mohammed Afzal, Koen Dercksen, Nils Dycke, Alexander Goldberg, Tom Hope, Dirk Hovy, Jonathan K. Kummerfeld, Anne Lauscher, Kevin Leyton-Brown, Sheng Lu, Mausam, Margot Mieskes, Aur'elie N'ev'eol, Danish Pruthi, Lizhen Qu, Roy Schwartz, Noah A. Smith, T. Solorio, Jingyan Wang, Xiaodan Zhu, Anna Rogers, Nihar B. Shah, Iryna Gurevych
Abstract summary: The paper discusses the potential for natural language processing to assist with the peer review process, including challenges and opportunities.

Title: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
Authors: Yixuan Weng, Minjun Zhu, Guangsheng Bao, Hongbo Zhang, Jindong Wang, Yue Zhang, Linyi Yang
Abstract summary: The paper demonstrates that large language models can surpass expert-level performance in research evaluation and generate papers that approach the quality of accepted papers.

Title: RelevAI-Reviewer: A Benchmark on AI Reviewers for Survey Paper Relevance
Authors: Paulo Henrique Couto, Quang Phuoc Ho, Nageeta Kumari, B. K. Rachmat, Thanh Gia Hieu Khuong, Ihsan Ullah, Lisheng Sun-Hosoya
Abstract summary: The paper proposes an AI system called RelevAI-Reviewer to assess the relevance of survey papers to a given prompt, as a step towards automating the peer review process.

Title: Human-in-the-Loop AI Reviewing: Feasibility, Opportunities, and Risks
Authors: Iddo Drori, Dov Te’eni
Abstract summary: AI-augmented peer review is feasible but has risks that need to be managed, as it is not yet accurate enough to fully replace human review.

Title: Exploring the potential of ChatGPT in the peer review process: An observational study.
Authors: Ahmed Saad, N. Jenko, S. Ariyaratne, Nick Birch, K. Iyengar, A. M. Davies, Raju Vaishya, R. Botchu
Abstract summary: ChatGPT can complement human peer review but is not yet suitable to fully automate the process.

Title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Large Language Models in Automating Academic Peer Reviews
Authors: Weimin Zhao, Q. Mahmoud
Venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
Abstract summary: Large language models can generate peer reviews for academic papers, but their quality is variable and they tend to be more positive than human-written reviews.

Title: GPT4 is Slightly Helpful for Peer-Review Assistance: A Pilot Study
Authors: Zachary Robertson
Abstract summary: GPT4 can provide peer review assistance, though its helpfulness is only slightly comparable to human reviewers.

Title: Equity in Scientific Publishing: Can Artificial Intelligence Transform the Peer Review Process?
Authors: C. Sabet, S. Bajaj, F. C. Stanford, L. Celi
Abstract summary: Using AI like ChatGPT for peer review could help address inequities in the research process, but AI has limitations that need to be addressed through human oversight and collaboration.

Title: Artificial intelligence to support publishing and peer review: A summary and review
Authors: K. Kousha, M. Thelwall
Abstract summary: The paper summarizes the current state of AI technology to support publishing and peer review, noting that automation can be useful for finding reviewers and initial quality control, but the value of AI for reviewing itself has not been clearly demonstrated.

Title: ChatGPT and the Future of Journal Reviews: A Feasibility Study
Authors: Som Biswas, Dushyant Dobaria, Harris L. Cohen
Venue: The Yale Journal of Biology and Medicine
Abstract summary: This study explores the feasibility of using ChatGPT as an AI reviewer for academic journals, finding it can provide useful feedback comparable to human reviewers.

Title: Unveiling the Sentinels: Assessing AI Performance in Cybersecurity Peer Review
Authors: Liang Niu, Nian Xue, Christina Pöpper
Abstract summary: The paper evaluates the performance of AI models, including ChatGPT and Doc2Vec, in predicting the outcomes of peer review for cybersecurity research papers, finding the Doc2Vec-based approach performs significantly better.

Title: Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers? A large-scale empirical analysis
Authors: Weixin Liang, Yuhui Zhang, Hancheng Cao, Binglu Wang, Daisy Ding, Xinyu Yang, Kailas Vodrahalli, Siyu He, D. Smith, Yian Yin, Daniel A. McFarland, James Zou
Abstract summary: Large language models like GPT-4 can provide useful feedback on research papers, with overlap in points raised compared to human peer reviewers, and researchers find it more beneficial than some human reviewers.

Title: ReviewerGPT? An Exploratory Study on Using Large Language Models for Paper Reviewing
Authors: Ryan Liu, Nihar B. Shah
Abstract summary: Large language models like GPT-4 show promise for assisting in specific paper reviewing tasks like identifying errors, but struggle with more holistic paper evaluations.

Title: ChatGPT for (Finance) Research: The Bananarama Conjecture
Authors: M. Dowling, B. Lucey
Abstract summary: ChatGPT can assist with finance research, but has limitations in literature synthesis and developing testing frameworks, and the quality depends on input data and researcher expertise.

Title: Peer Prediction for Peer Review: Designing a Marketplace for Ideas
Authors: A. Ugarov
Abstract summary: The paper proposes a platform to facilitate academic peer review using peer prediction algorithms to improve accuracy and timeliness.

Title: Funding agencies say no to AI peer review
Authors: J. Kaiser
Abstract summary: Funding agencies are concerned about using AI for peer review due to issues with confidentiality, accuracy, and "originality of thought".

Title: The researchers using AI to analyse peer review
Authors: Richard van Noorden
Abstract summary: The paper describes a study using machine learning to assess the quality of peer review reports.

Title: Challenges, experiments, and computational solutions in peer review
Authors: Nihar B. Shah
Abstract summary: This paper does not directly address the use of AI for peer review or how it compares to human experts.

Title: Artificial intelligence technologies to support research assessment: A review
Authors: K. Kousha, M. Thelwall
Abstract summary: This review examines how AI technologies can be used to support research assessment, including predicting citation counts and quality scores.

Title: Predicting article quality scores with machine learning: The U.K. Research Excellence Framework
Authors: M. Thelwall, K. Kousha, Mahshid Abdoli, Emma Stuart, Meiko Makita, Paul Wilson, Jonathan M. Levitt, Petr Knoth, Matteo Cancellieri
Abstract summary: Machine learning can predict article quality scores in medical, physical sciences, and economics, but not as well in other fields.

Title: Between Acceptance and Rejection: Challenges for an Automatic Peer Review Process
Authors: G. Fernandes, Pedro O. S. Vaz de Melo
Venue: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
Abstract summary: Current AI models can help editors decide whether to approve or reject a paper, but are not yet capable of fully automating the peer review process.

Title: DeepASPeer: Towards an Aspect-level Sentiment Controllable Framework for Decision Prediction from Academic Peer Reviews
Authors: Sandeep Kumar, Hardik Arora, Tirthankar Ghosal, Asif Ekbal
Venue: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
Abstract summary: The paper proposes a deep neural architecture that uses review text, aspect categories, and sentiment to predict the final peer review decision with up to 76.67% accuracy.

Title: Is the future of peer review automated?
Authors: Robert Schulz, A. Barnett, René Bernard, Nicholas J L Brown, Jennifer A. Byrne, P. Eckmann, M. A. Gazda, H. Kilicoglu, Eric M. Prager, M. Salholz-Hillel, G. ter Riet, Timothy H. Vines, Colby J. Vorland, Han Zhuang, A. Bandrowski, T. Weissgerber
Abstract summary: Automated screening tools can enhance peer review by identifying issues, but cannot replace human editors and reviewers in assessing overall quality and fit.

Title: Incorporating Training, Self-monitoring and AI-Assistance to Improve Peer Feedback Quality
Authors: A. Darvishi, Hassan Khosravi, Solmaz Abdi, S. Sadiq, D. Gašević
Abstract summary: This paper examines a peer review approach that integrates training, self-monitoring, and AI quality-control to improve the quality of peer feedback, but does not address AI's ability to peer review research.

Title: AI-assisted peer review
Authors: Alessandro Checco, L. Bracciale, P. Loreti, S. Pinfield, G. Bianchi
Abstract summary: The paper discusses the potential and pitfalls of using AI to assist or approximate human peer review of research, including concerns about algorithmic bias.

Title: PEERAssist: Leveraging on Paper-Review Interactions to Predict Peer Review Decisions
Authors: P. Bharti, Shashi Ranjan, Tirthankar Ghosal, Mayank Agrawal, Asif Ekbal
Venue: International Conference on Asian Digital Libraries
Abstract summary: The paper proposes an AI-powered system to assist in the peer review process by predicting review decisions based on paper-review interactions.

Title: Can We Automate Scientific Reviewing?
Authors: Weizhe Yuan, Pengfei Liu, Graham Neubig
Abstract summary: Current AI systems can generate comprehensive but less constructive and factual peer reviews compared to humans, highlighting challenges in automating scientific reviewing.

Title: A Synthetic Prediction Market for Estimating Confidence in Published Work
Authors: S. Rajtmajer, Christopher Griffin, Jian Wu, Robert Fraleigh, Laxmaan Balaji, A. Squicciarini, A. Kwasnica, David M. Pennock, Michael Mclaughlin, Timothy Fritton, Nishanth Nakshatri, A. Menon, Sai Ajay Modukuri, Rajal Nivargi, Xin Wei, C. Lee Giles
Abstract summary: A synthetic prediction market is developed to assess the credibility of published claims in the social and behavioral sciences.

Title: Academics evaluating academics: a methodology to inform the review process on top of open citations
Authors: Federica Bologna, A. Iorio, S. Peroni, Francesco Poggi
Abstract summary: The paper proposes a methodology to explore whether citation-based metrics can provide insights into how human peer-review is conducted in research assessment exercises.

Title: Estimating the deep replicability of scientific findings using human and artificial intelligence
Authors: Yang Yang, Youyou Wu, Brian Uzzi
Venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
Abstract summary: An AI model can predict the replicability of scientific findings as well as or better than human experts, using the paper text rather than just reported statistics.

Title: Artificial intelligence, drug repurposing and peer review
Authors: Jeremy M. Levin, Tudor I. Oprea, S. Davidovich, T. Clozel, John P. Overington, Q. Vanhaelen, Charles R. Cantor, E. Bischof, A. Zhavoronkov
Abstract summary: The paper discusses whether AI can help compensate for inadequate peer review of drug-repurposing papers during an infodemic, but does not address AI's ability to peer review academic economics research.

Title: When expert recommendation contradicts peer opinion: Relative social influence of valence, group identity and artificial intelligence
Authors: Jinping Wang, Maria D. Molina, S. S. Sundar
Abstract summary: AI systems can be as influential as human experts in providing online recommendations, suggesting AI could substitute for human peer review.

Title: Automatically detecting open academic review praise and criticism
Authors: M. Thelwall, Eleanor-Rose Papas, Zena Nyakoojo, L. Allen, Verena Weigert
Abstract summary: PeerJudge, an AI-based sentiment analysis tool, can predict peer review decisions from negative comments but not positive comments.

Title: ReviewRobot: Explainable Paper Review Generation based on Knowledge Synthesis
Authors: Qingyun Wang, Qi Zeng, Lifu Huang, Kevin Knight, Heng Ji, Nazneen Rajani
Venue: International Conference on Natural Language Generation
Abstract summary: ReviewRobot can automatically generate valid and constructive paper reviews by synthesizing knowledge from the target paper, cited papers, and a background corpus.

Title: DeepSentiPeer: Harnessing Sentiment in Review Texts to Recommend Peer Review Decisions
Authors: Tirthankar Ghosal, Rajeev Verma, Asif Ekbal, P. Bhattacharyya
Venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Abstract summary: An AI system can predict peer review outcomes by analyzing sentiment in review texts, potentially assisting editors when reviewers are missing.

Title: Artificial Intelligence, Automation and Peer Review
Authors: M. Thelwall
Abstract summary: AI-based peer review could introduce biases against authors from non-English speaking and less-resourced countries, which would need to be addressed through bias correction factors.

Title: A Dataset of Peer Reviews (PeerRead): Collection, Insights and NLP Applications
Authors: Dongyeop Kang, Bridger Waleed Ammar, Bhavana Dalvi, Madeleine van Zuylen, Sebastian Kohlmeier, E. Hovy, Roy Schwartz
Venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Abstract summary: The paper introduces a dataset of peer reviews that can be used to study peer review processes and develop NLP models to predict acceptance decisions and review aspect scores.

Title: The Impact of Machine Learning on Economics
Authors: S. Athey
Abstract summary: This paper provides an overview of the early contributions and future potential of machine learning in economics, but does not specifically address its use in peer-reviewing research.

Title: Can your paper evade the editors axe? Towards an AI assisted peer review system
Authors: Tirthankar Ghosal, Rajeev Verma, Asif Ekbal, S. Saha, P. Bhattacharyya, Srinivasa Satya Sameer Kumar Chivukula, G. Tsatsaronis, Pascal Coupet, M. Gregory
Abstract summary: This paper explores the feasibility of an AI-assisted peer review system that can predict desk rejections of papers based on factors like scope and quality.

Title: Juxtapeer: Comparative Peer Review Yields Higher Quality Feedback and Promotes Deeper Reflection
Authors: Julia Cambre, S. Klemmer, Chinmay Kulkarni
Venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
Abstract summary: Comparative peer review helps learners write better feedback, but the paper does not address AI's ability to peer review research.

Title: AI peer reviewers unleashed to ease publishing grind
Authors: D. Heaven
Abstract summary: This article does not provide a research study or findings, but rather discusses the use of AI for peer review to ease the publishing process.

Title: Algorithmically outsourcing the detection of statistical errors and other problems
Authors: J. Wren
Abstract summary: Algorithms can be used to detect statistical errors and other technical problems in scientific manuscripts before publication, potentially improving peer review.

Title: Computational support for academic peer review
Authors: Simon Price, Peter A. Flach
Abstract summary: This paper discusses computational tools for supporting academic peer review, but does not provide specific details on AI's capabilities in this area.

Title: , S., & Flach, P. (2017). Computational support for academic peer review: a perspective from artificial intelligence. Communications of the ACM , 60 (3), 70-79. https:
Authors: Peter A. Flach
Abstract summary: AI tools can automate parts of the peer review process, but opportunities remain to improve the peer review process through persistent reviewer and author profiles.

Title: Prediction of Grades for Reviewing with Automated Peer-review and Reputation Metrics
Authors: Da Young Lee, Ferry Pramudianto, E. Gehringer
Abstract summary: The paper develops a model to predict student peer review grades using automated metrics and reviewer reputation, but does not address AI peer review of academic research.

Title: Big names or big ideas: Do peer-review panels select the best science proposals?
Authors: Danielle Li, Leila Agha
Abstract summary: Peer review panels at the NIH are effective at predicting the future quality of proposed research based on publication, citation, and patenting outcomes.

Title: Measuring the effectiveness of scientific gatekeeping
Authors: Kyle Siler, Kirby P. Lee, L. Bero
Venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
Abstract summary: Peer review generally identifies quality manuscripts, but editors and reviewers sometimes reject highly cited papers, suggesting limitations in their ability to recognize the most impactful research.

Title: Predicting Source Code Quality with Static Analysis and Machine Learning
Authors: Vera Barstad, M. G. Olsen, Terje Gjøsæter
Abstract summary: This paper investigates using static analysis and machine learning to predict source code quality, but does not address AI peer review of academic research.

Title: Tuned Models of Peer Assessment in MOOCs
Authors: C. Piech, Jonathan Huang, Zhenghao Chen, Chuong B. Do, A. Ng, D. Koller
Abstract summary: This paper develops algorithms to estimate and correct for biases and reliabilities in peer grading in MOOCs, improving accuracy compared to human experts.

Title: Automatically Predicting Peer-Review Helpfulness
Authors: Wenting Xiong, D. Litman
Venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Abstract summary: The paper shows that machine learning can predict the helpfulness of peer reviews using structural, textual, and peer-review specific features.

Title: An algorithm for automated rating of reviewers
Authors: Tracy Riggs, R. Wilensky
Venue: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
Abstract summary: The paper proposes an algorithm that could automatically rate reviewers and incorporate reviewer quality into assessing paper merit, as an alternative to traditional peer review.
